items.title: The Lost Camp
items.description: Three boys at a sleep‑away camp stumble upon an abandoned town haunted by a vengeful spirit. As they explore, the ghost’s wrath escalates, forcing them to confront personal loss and survive the terror. The story blends supernatural horror with teenage drama.

items.title: It’s a Double Date a Classic
items.description: Jess and Katie, two friends living in the 1930s, feel trapped by the monotony of their era. They decide to go on a double date that promises excitement, but the night forces them to confront personal sacrifices. The story explores whether the thrill is worth the cost. It blends period detail with emotional tension.

items.title: A Long Time Coming
items.description:
Award-winning Director Keith Lakean Powell Presents A Long Time Coming is a gritty, independent mid-19th-century Western epic that explores a shifting lawless frontier where outlaws and Native Americans roam wild, and an expanding government fiercely struggles to impose institutional civilization upon the land. 

The narrative centers on a heavy moral divergence, tracking a fractured brotherhood between two notorious outlaws and the contrasting paths they choose when tested by greed and duty.

items.title: CAESAR III JUDGEMENT
items.description: Chief Anthony Abiola returns in 1980 California as power, family and betrayal collide. A ruthless war spreads across continents, forcing loyalties to shift and deadly decisions to be made. The story blends crime drama with a legacy‑driven saga, culminating in a high‑stakes showdown.

items.title: Curtain Call
items.description: Curtain Call follows a single night of violent power struggle within a criminal organization, where loyalty is demanded and betrayal is punished. The short film depicts a coordinated purge as the leader seeks to restore order, culminating in a tense showdown that explores dominance and consequence.

items.title: Tears of Steel (2012)
items.description: Tears of Steel (code-named Project Mango) is a short science fiction film by producer Ton Roosendaal and director/writer Ian Hubert. The film is both live-action and CGI; it was made using new enhancements to the visual effects capabilities of Blender, a free and open-source 3D computer graphics app. Set in a dystopian future, the short film features a group of warriors and scientists who gather at the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam in a desperate attempt to save the world from destructive robots. Rights: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (CC BY 3.0). Credit: Blender Foundation.

items.title: Big Buck Bunny (2008)
items.description: Big Buck Bunny is a comedy about a well-tempered rabbit "Big Buck", who finds his day spoiled by the rude actions of the forest bullies, three rodents. In the typical 1950ies cartoon tradition Big Buck then prepares for the rodents a comical revenge. Rights: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (CC BY 3.0). Credit: Blender Foundation.

items.title: Sintel (2010)
items.description: A girl named Sintel searches for a baby dragon she calls Scales. A flashback reveals that Sintel found Scales with its wing injured and helped care for it, forming a close bond with it. By the time its wing recovered and it was able to fly, Scales was caught by an adult dragon. Sintel has since embarked on a quest to rescue Scales, fending off beasts and warriors along the way. She eventually comes across a cave housing an adult and baby dragon, the latter of which she believes to be Scales. The adult dragon discovers and attacks Sintel, but hesitates to kill her. Sintel slays the dragon, only to recognize the scar on its wing and realize the dragon is an adult Scales, and that she too has aged considerably. Sintel leaves the cave heartbroken, unknowingly followed by Scales's baby. Rights: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 (CC BY 3.0). Credit: Blender Foundation.
